resources.string: Uses the volume keys in place of tapping and scrolling the screen

For when touching the screen is difficult: a short press of a volume key scrolls the screen one page at a time, or taps a position you set in advance. It helps when reading one-handed or lying down, or when finger movement is limited.

A long press still adjusts the volume as usual.

This app does not read what is shown on the screen. It has no permission to access the internet, so no information is ever sent off the device.
To use volumetap, turn on its accessibility service in your device settings.

On this device, power saving stops volumetap in the background, so the volume keys sometimes stop working.

Please change these two settings:
• In App info → “Power”, choose “No restrictions”
• In device Settings → “Apps” → “Background autostart” (at the top), turn on volumetap

Changing these turns accessibility off for a moment. When you are done, turn volumetap back on in Accessibility.

(Menu names may differ by device.)
Short press = next page / Long press = volume
Swipe back to the previous screen
Used for apps you haven\'t added (including the home screen). If you choose swiping here, the home screen, maps and so on will move too, so it is better to add each app you use.
No apps added yet. Use “Add app” to choose the apps you want to page through.
Swipes up the screen to scroll to the next screen.
Swipes down the screen to go back one screen. Near the top of a list, some apps treat this as “pull to refresh” and reload the list.
No position is set, so this key still adjusts the volume for now
Set it while holding the device upright for portrait, or sideways for landscape.
Turn on volumetap in Accessibility to set positions on the app.
Tap the position\nyou want the key to tap
💡 For Google Discover, choose “Google”. The Discover feed to the left of the home screen also belongs to the Google app (“Google News” is a different app).
💡 PWAs (web apps added to the home screen) don\'t appear in this list. They run in the browser, so to use yomikake or similar, choose your browser, such as Chrome.
While paused, the volume keys work as usual. You can also switch this from the Quick Settings tile.
A short press of a volume button scrolls the screen one page at a time, or taps a position you set. A long press still adjusts the volume. No ads, no purchases, no network access.

Opens the app so you can adjust the position and distance on its actual screen. The result is saved for the current orientation (portrait or landscape).
Turn on volumetap in Accessibility to adjust.
Adjusting the swipe for %1$s. Open a screen to adjust, such as a long page, then tap “Start”.
○ Start moves the whole line. ● End changes the distance (shared by next and prev). Scrolling more than the visible area skips lines.
The test didn\'t go through. Tap “Test” again.
Adjustment stopped because you left the app
Adjustment stopped because the screen rotated
Adjustment stopped because the screen turned off
Setting where %2$s taps in %1$s. Open the screen with the button you want to press, then tap “Start”.
Tap the position you want. Keep your finger down and move it to fine-tune.
